title: PHASE 0 go/no-go: recover the ncclNet_vN ABI and get a plugin accepted
VERDICT: NO-GO under the bead's own gate, with a bounded cause and a named next step.
gate_as_stated: SUCCESS is NCCL loading an intentionally minimal plugin AND REPORTING it, with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO output naming the plugin and the accepted ABI version. Anything less is NO-GO.
what_the_gate_asked_for: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO naming the plugin and an accepted version
what_happened: NCCL read NCCL_NET_PLUGIN, resolved ncclNetPlugin_v11 WITHOUT a dlsym failure, invoked it, and then died with SIGSEGV (exit 139) reading past the end of a deliberately two-member struct. It never got as far as reporting a plugin.
jobs: 20261002t185121-d61c6fa5 first attempt, no cudart on the library path
20261002t185822-8946b525 entry point compiled, probe ran 1.0s with an EMPTY log
20261002t190121-f351522f stdbuf -o0 -e0, which is what made the crash legible

env_var.evidence: NCCL INFO ENV/Plugin: NCCL_NET_PLUGIN set by environment to <path>
env_var.confirms_bead: the bead's warning is right -- NCCL_PLUGIN would not have worked

entry_symbol.evidence: NCCL INFO ncclOsDlsym(ncclNetPlugin_v11) failed: undefined symbol: ncclNetPlugin_v11 -- and with that symbol supplied there is NO failure line at all, which is how the successful resolution is known
entry_symbol.note: The binary carries ncclNetPluginInit / ncclNetPluginFinalize / ncclNetPluginInitialized / ncclNetPluginStateInitReady as strings, which is where the entry name came from. The first plugin guessed ncclNetGetDevCount_vN from the public API shape and was rejected; the loader's own log is what corrected it.

probe_order.source: the order of the ncclOsDlsym failure lines, one per version

max_version_is_v11_NOT_v12.finding: The loader probes v11 down to v6 and NEVER v12, even though ncclNet_v12_t, ncclNetDeviceHandle_v12_t and ncclNetPlugin_v12 all exist in the binary.
max_version_is_v11_NOT_v12.consequence: The bead's premise 'the loader probes ncclNet_v6 through ncclNet_v12' is wrong at the top end. Targeting v12 would waste the work.
max_version_is_v11_NOT_v12.note: This is recorded rather than quietly worked around: it is exactly the kind of premise error that a plausible struct built on it would have inherited.

struct_is_larger_than_two_members.finding: With ncclNetPlugin_v11 exported and returning a two-member struct, NCCL segfaults rather than rejecting the plugin.
struct_is_larger_than_two_members.inference: the loader reads past member 2, so the struct layout is load-bearing and must be recovered rather than guessed
struct_is_larger_than_two_members.how_it_is_known: no dlsym failure line precedes the crash, so the symbol resolved; the fault is therefore inside the call or immediately after it, not a failed load

PREMISE_VERIFIED_BEFORE_TRUSTING_IT.conclusion: the bead's premise holds exactly as stated; the ABI is not in the header and not exported

RECOVERED_FROM_THE_BINARY.bead_correction: The bead says to group the strings by a P/E suffix. THAT IS NOT TRUE OF THIS BUILD: not one of the 148 ncclNet* strings carries a P or E suffix. Grouping by it yields nothing, so the grouping step was replaced by grouping by TYPE NAME (ncclNet_vN_t, ncclNetProperties_vN_t, ...), which is present and usable.
RECOVERED_FROM_THE_BINARY.strings_artifact: the leading digits on entries like '12ncclNet_v6_t' are string-table offsets bleeding into `strings` output, not part of the name

WHY_NO_STRUCT_WAS_WRITTEN.rule_followed: the bead forbids writing a struct from memory of the public plugin API
WHY_NO_STRUCT_WAS_WRITTEN.what_i_wrote_instead: a struct containing ONLY the two function pointers the loader must reach, with the remainder deliberately undefined
WHY_NO_STRUCT_WAS_WRITTEN.why_that_is_the_honest_thing: a struct guessed from the public API would have compiled, would probably have been accepted, and would have been a plausible interface resting on nothing. The two-member struct instead FAILS LOUDLY, which is the outcome that carries information.
WHY_NO_STRUCT_WAS_WRITTEN.the_only_unrecovered_thing: ncclNetPlugin_v11's SIGNATURE (what argument it takes). Everything else -- the entry name, the version list, the probe order, the env var -- was recovered from the binary or the loader's own log.

NEXT_STEP_NAMED.what: resolve the DWARF DEFINITION DIEs for ncclNet_v11_t, not the forward declarations
NEXT_STEP_NAMED.evidence_it_is_possible: the library DOES carry .debug_info, .debug_abbrev, .debug_line, .debug_loc and .debug_ranges, so the struct layout is recoverable from this binary without guessing
NEXT_STEP_NAMED.what_i_reached: pyelftools finds ncclNet_v11_t, ncclNet_v12_t, ncclNetCommConfig_v11_t and ncclNetProperties_v11_t, but only as FORWARD DECLARATIONS -- DIEs with a DW_AT_name and no children and no DW_AT_byte_size. The definitions are not where a name-first search lands.
NEXT_STEP_NAMED.next: walk DW_AT_specification / DW_AT_abstract_origin edges and re-iterate every CU rather than stopping at the first named DIE, then read DW_AT_byte_size and the ordered DW_AT_data_member_location of the definition.
NEXT_STEP_NAMED.why_it_matters: this is the difference between a NO-GO that redirects the epic and a GO. The bead is explicit that a NO-GO is worth more than a plausible struct on a guess -- but a NO-GO issued while DWARF is sitting unexhausted in the binary would be the wrong kind of no-go, and it should say so.

WHAT_A_GO_WOULD_STILL_REQUIRE: even with the layout, the plugin must then return a non-zero device count from ncclNetGetDevCount and a usable ncclNetDeviceHandle, which means recovering ncclNetProperties_v11_t as well. Phase 0's gate is a MINIMAL plugin, so a zero-device plugin may already be enough IF the loader reports it rather than faulting.
MISTAKES_OF_MINE_IN_THIS_BEAD: the first probe used torch but never issued a COLLECTIVE, so the net-plugin init path was never entered and the run reported SUCCESS while testing nothing -- a green result from a program that did not do the thing. Replaced with a C program calling ncclAllReduce directly.

the first plugin exported ncclNetGetDevCount_vN from the public API shape; the loader wanted ncclNetPlugin_vN. Writing the struct from memory -- which the bead forbids -- would have produced the same wrong answer with more confidence in it.

the first plugin crash produced an EMPTY log and I nearly read that as 'nothing happened'. It was stdout buffering: the crash discarded the buffer. stdbuf -o0 -e0 is what made the fault legible, and it is the difference between 'it did not run' and 'it ran and died'.
ncclCommInitRank(comm, nranks, commId, rank) was called with the rank in the commId slot; the compiler caught it, which is a better outcome than a probe that never brought up a communicator.
